explicit_definitions_given: Intrinsic justification: based on intuition or self-evidence
Extrinsic justification: based on empirical success or indispensability

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Acknowledges objections but argues they are less damaging than the alternative
objections_raised: Maddy's compromise fails to resolve conflicts between intrinsic and extrinsic evidence
All three possible resolutions (intrinsic, extrinsic, neither) lead to unacceptable consequences

appeals_to_authority: Quine, Putnam, Godel, Maddy, Zermelo, Hebb
method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Philosophical argumentation, thought experiments, historical examples
named_thought_experiments: Axiom of Choice and Banach-Tarski paradox

philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Critical, realist-leaning but skeptical of compromise

structural_organization.structure_type: Problem-solution-critique with historical exposition and counterexample-based trilemma

summary_of_core_decisions: The text critiques Maddy's compromise Platonism by showing that when intrinsic and extrinsic evidence conflict, all three possible resolutions (intrinsic, extrinsic, neither) lead to the same criticisms that motivated the compromise. Thus, the compromise fails to solve the fundamental problem of weighing different types of mathematical justification.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Negative: argues against a specific position
